dispositions.justification: Retains the post-baseline shared-contract disposition. Condensed guidance preserves global font, color and padding bounds; inspection and host-controlled automatic application remain separate from authoring.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Compact guidance preserves exact label targets, typography keys, contextual dimensions and protected bindings; binding-related patch keys remain excluded from automatic application.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Original section slots, identifier constraints, static write-in content and contextual dimensions remain documented; added fields still pass binding and scope validation.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Existing targets remain required, independent tables must retain a column, and removed protected identities remain checked if reinstated. Bound-field removal remains manual.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Original-slot restrictions and context identities remain documented; the host still requires the complete unique current identity set and enforces selected scope.
Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Compact guidance preserves supported section properties, non-items grid targets, header restrictions and the prohibition on whole-table keepTogether.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. The guide still requires all five original sections and places a repeating header first; schema uniqueness, scope checks and final design validation remain.
Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Paper, margins, custom dimensions and user-supplied printer constraints remain documented; page changes remain outside the automatic-operation allowlist.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Existing asset identity or value:null remains required; the guide preserves default-mark removal and distinguishes actual visibility from a null asset identifier.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Primary collection selection still uses available absolute array paths; additional collections remain human-only, protected bindings remain enforced, and automatic application is excluded.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Both schema and compact guide preserve stored-text-only semantics, explicit header enablement for visible Blank titles, and the prohibition on widening heading-only scope.

Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. The compact guide preserves items-only rowBackground, six-digit color or null, stripe-preference preservation and whole-table scope; this operation remains auto-eligible after required checks.

Retains the changed shared-contract closure. Supported heading and page-number targets, typography bounds, inheritance and empty-override clearing remain documented without granting cross-target scope or direct commit authority.

The changed shared guide supports context-first design discovery, and handlers impose no capability-first prerequisite. The registry description still says Call this first; that stale sequencing instruction is the reported P2.

The bundled loader now returns condensed form, general-print and workflow guidance. Reading a guide still establishes answer evidence without granting additional effects, source access or disclosure authorization.

The design prompt now begins with context rather than capability discovery. Context still supplies authoring identities, binding catalog, selected-target rules, measured typography, run limits and host-selected commit policy.

Changed shared guidance preserves typed private-draft operations, the per-call operation limit and combined patches. Host parsing, scope and binding guards remain; successful edits invalidate prior inspection and observation evidence.

The condensed guide retains exact-final-candidate inspection, receipt identity, edit and undo invalidation, and readiness limitations. Finish still requires the latest ready inspection rather than a guide or scenario result.

Changed guidance retains optional one-run text disclosure, synthetic-value policy, separate pixel permission and authorization expiry. Semantic observation still clears final inspection, requiring a subsequent inspect_draft before finish.

Changed guidance preserves the latest observation identifier, zero-based page index, bounded crop, independent fictional pixel authorization and paired host PNG. Cropping grants no sensitive-data bypass or visual-acceptance claim.

The condensed guide retains synthetic row scenarios, custom-path limitations and the absence of observation receipts. Scenario results remain answer evidence but cannot replace active-candidate inspection required by finish.

Changed shared guidance still describes private-step retraction and invalidation even when content is restored. The handler clears source handoff and inspection evidence; completion requires fresh inspection.

Changed guidance retains replacement rather than append semantics, bounded run-local memory and recording image observations before expiry. Notes grant no additional authoring, disclosure, source or commit authority.

Changed shared guidance preserves successful exact-final inspection and separates proposal delivery from host application. The handler still requires current ready evidence and, for coding grants, current imported artifact lineage.

Changed guidance permits context-grounded answers without capability discovery. Exact message preservation, the character bound, latest-receipt checks and the distinction between answered completion and proposal delivery remain.

Changed prompt and guide preserve public bounded assistant-reported blockers. The shared commit policy explicitly prevents treating ordinary human Preview and Apply requirements as missing capabilities or blockers.

The shared knowledge dependency changed, while source-specific guidance remains unchanged. Listing still requires the run-owned fictional workspace authorization and grants no host filesystem access or automatic source application.

The changed shared guide does not expand source authority. Bounded UTF-8 reads remain lease-authorized and explicitly untrusted; source-workspace guidance still distinguishes fictional source consent from business-value disclosure.

The shared knowledge dependency changed without changing bounded source-search parameters or authorization. Search remains restricted to the supplied fictional workspace and cannot grant form edits, disclosure or commit permission.

The changed shared guide retains separate host-paired source authority. Existing-file writes require exact read digests, creation uses null expectedDigest, and source writes never directly change the live form.

The shared knowledge dependency changed while source-specific atomic patch instructions remain. Exact digests, null creation and deletion semantics, authorization and manual source application remain distinct from ordinary design automation.

Changed shared guidance grants no commands by itself. The unchanged source guide and tool schema retain isolated network-denied execution, root cwd semantics and independent-acceptance limits. Runtime execution is UNVERIFIED.

The changed shared guide does not alter source diff authority. Diff remains a bounded read against the original fictional starter, not approval, artifact acceptance or permission to apply source-derived changes automatically.

The shared knowledge dependency changed without removing source artifact requirements. Retrieval still names a successful current command and returns a host-bound opaque descriptor rather than execution or application permission.

Changed shared guidance preserves private-draft authoring and final inspection. Verified artifact operations still pass through draft.apply, invalidate observation and inspection evidence, and remain subject to explicit human source application.

The guide is directly condensed and now starts with context. Operation constraints, binding protection, scope, disclosure, final inspection and automatic versus manual commit boundaries remain available in guidance, schemas and context.

The generator groups workflows by shared path or reason while retaining each feature name and status category. Human-mediated, adapter-missing and host-only workflows remain non-tools without expanded execution authority.

The guide is directly condensed while retaining independent-table operation limits, exact barcode requirements, currency and supplied-source facts, human import paths and share-copy disclosure boundaries.

The source guide text is unchanged in batch 15, but its shared knowledge-loader closure changed. Source consent, genuine leases, current artifact lineage, exact inspection and explicit human application remain required.
